summary: Oconto County lookout in the Nicolet National Forest: a 1934 survey refers to it, a 1990 note calls it old, and the FFLOS lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the FFLOS index. A 1990 survey note refers to the old tower and a concrete pier of it, not to a standing structure.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey set a concrete monument and described it by reference to the lookout and a lookout keeper's house; land given as Forest Service
Fifteen Mystery Week campers visited the lookout; the 100-foot spire was climbed by ladder in groups of three, per The Post-Crescent as quoted by the lookout site
Recovery note mentions a concrete pier of the old fire tower; survey station placed near the location of the old lookout tower; land owned by Wisconsin Department of Transportation

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 description puts the monument on Forest Service land; the 1990 recovery note names the Wisconsin Department of Transportation as owner. The notes do not explain the change, and the lookout's own land status is not stated in any source.

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, design, staffing roster, fire record or removal date found in these sources. The 1938 item is known only as quoted on the Central US Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not checked. The NGS datasheet is the strongest source (1934 description, 1990 recovery note, 2003 condition check). The Nicolet National Forest history PDF (foresthistory.org) was searched and does not mention Boulder Lake. Brief record checked: height 30.5 m matches the 100-foot spire; county and status match; no correction proposed. Story runs about 240 words.
